title: Ticket Number Forty-One
subject: A man pawns his guitar to buy his wife a ring, and the pawnbroker lets him play it every Sunday before the shop opens
caption: Russian-bard-style acoustic guitar poetry in English, kitchen-table storytelling. Single nylon-string guitar with steady arpeggio verses and strummed Am-E7 choruses, occasional bass-string thumb runs, sparse low male harmony on the last line of each chorus. Dry close-miked room, no reverb tail, soft finger noise. Male baritone, plain warm voice, unhurried storytelling phrasing. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, A minor. Wry and tender. No drums, no synths, no strings, no autotune, no rapping, no pop polish.
lyrics:
[Intro - nylon guitar arpeggio]

[Verse 1]
I carried it in wrapped in a coat
Past the bakery, past the bank
The man behind the glass said
Forty pounds, and here's your stub

[Chorus]
Forty-one, forty-one
Hang it on the hook
I will come on Sunday
Before the shutters rise

[Verse 2]
The pawnbroker is a quiet man
He wiped the strings with his sleeve
Said it still holds the pitch
Better than my ledgers do

[Verse 3]
Now the ring is on her finger
Plain and thin, it fits her well
She asks me where I go on Sundays
I say to see an old friend

[Chorus]
Forty-one, forty-one
He lets me hold the neck
She came along last Sunday
And she asked me for a waltz

[Outro - nylon guitar, slow strum]
Forty-one, forty-one
Sunday, at nine
